sentences.text: Dhaval Kakkad vs State Of Rajashthan on 14 June, 2024

Author: Vikram Nath
Bench: Vikram Nath
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No.2771 of 2024
 (Arising out of Slp (Crl.) No. 7915 of 2024)
 Dhaval Kakkad .... Appellan
 Versus
 State Of Rajasthan & Anr. .... Respondent(
 Order
Leave granted.

This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 14th May, 2024 passed by the Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court whereby the application of the appellant for grant of anticipatory bail in FIR No.0111 of 2023 registered at Sanjay Circle Police Station, District Jaipur City (North)
under Sections 420 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 has been rejected.

entities.text: Sanjay Circle Police Station, District Jaipur City
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
This Court on 10.06.2024 had passed the following order:
Learned counsel for the petitioner states that the petitioner has already returned the substantial amount of Rs.40,00,000/
 (Rupees forty lakhs only) approximately and is ready and willing to pay the balance amount of Rs.20,00,000/
 (Rupees twenty lakhs only), for which talks are going on between the parties and there is likelihood that tomorrow, i.e. 11th June, 2024, a settlement may be arrived at.
Let this matter be listed on 14.06.2024.

Reason:
Till then, the petitioner may not be arrested.
The petitioner may also implead the complainant in the meantime and also serve copy of this order on the complainant within 24 hours.
Before this Court a joint application has been filed bearing Criminal MP No.132546 of 2024 stating that a compromise has been entered into between the parties on 11.06.2024.
Along with it photostat copies of the said agreement and also the copies of the bank drafts of Rs.20 lakhs paid by the appellant to the respondent no.2 have been filed.

sentences.text: The parties have prayed for quashing of the FIR in question in view of the settlement arrived at.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also taking into consideration the fact that the parties have compromised and any further investigation or trial would be an exercise in futility and only wasting time of the Court, we are inclined to allow the application and quash the FIR No.0111 of 2023.
Accordingly, exercising this Courts power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India in particular the facts and circumstances of the case, we quash the Fir No.0111 of 2023.
The appeal is allowed accordingly.
